To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the colon mucus layer is organized in a two layer model with an inner, stratification layer that is firmly attached to the epithelium and is approximately 50 mm in thickness.
the normal colon flora resides in the outer layer of the mucus and that the outer layer is organized by the Muc2 mucin.
MUC2 mucins form a large net like polymer that organizes the mucus layers in the colon and that the glycan array on the MUCs is a key factor in the selection and interaction with commensal bacteria.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular organization and functions of the two mucus layers in colon.
the organization of the colon mucus layers and their function as a selective habitat for the commensal colon flora.
the organization and composition of the colon mucus and its role for the commensal bacteria and the epithelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the colon mucus layer is organized by MUC2 and that the inner mucus layer protects the epithelial cell from the colon flora.

the MUC2 glycosylation pattern is the key for the colonization of the colon by a species specific commensal flora and that this glycosylation pattern may be an important factor to prevent the colonization with pathogenic bacteria and thus to prevent inflammatory bowel diseases.

the Mucus is a complex, highly organized structure that is essential for the colonization of the colon by the normal commensal flora, and that the MUC2 glycan array is essential for the establishment of the species specific commensal flora.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MUC2 glycosylation is an important factor for the colonization and maintenance of the normal intestinal flora.
the colon mucus is organized into two layers by the MUC mucin, and the outer layer is the habitat of a specific colon flora.
the MUC2 protein and its glycan array are the major factors in organizing the colon mucus and in determining the habitat of the normal flora.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mucus layer is not only an important barrier against pathogens but also a habitat for the colon microbiota, which is essential for the health of the host.
MUC2 mucins and their glycan arrays are important in the organization of the colon mucus, which is a prerequisite for a normal host microbial symbiosis.
MUC2 is the organizer of the colon mucus and that the outer mucus layer is the habitat of a species specific colon flora that is selected by the MUC 2 mucin.
